summary: Freeze the combined #81/#82 checkpoint transport contract before changing production: raw snapshot bytes must survive CJK/escaped-data chunk boundaries in both directions, malformed foreign/negative/fractional/out-of-range checkpoint chunks must be fatal, and a rejected malformed candidate must leave the prior committed snapshot restorable.
steps: Re-read the current v4 Host checkpoint_chunk receiver, result publication path, Host restore-frame builder, Python restore reader, and Python checkpoint chunk sender after #61 merged.

Froze the successor protocol direction: raw checkpoint bytes will use base64 in both directions, decoded-byte caps will remain authoritative, and the wire protocol version will bump rather than silently changing v4 semantics.

Added real-runtime RED coverage for CJK bytes crossing 128 KiB chunk boundaries, JSON escaping expansion, durable Host-to-kernel restore, and malformed chunk ownership/range checks preserving the previous snapshot.

evidence.note: Confirmed Python slices raw UTF-8 bytes then strict-decodes each chunk, Host slices raw bytes then independently toString('utf8'), and Host checkpoint_chunk validation lacks active-cell identity, safe-integer/range, duplicate/completeness, and aggregate-byte checks.
Production code is intentionally unchanged in this candidate; GitHub Actions will capture the baseline failures before the causal transport patch.

limitations: This record is RED-only evidence and does not claim the issues are fixed.
Durable crash consistency and permissions remain separate #71/#83 concerns even though durable restore is used as a test path here.
